Subject: Follow-up: inference economics — hyperscaler comparison and lab asks

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of lab tests so we can produce apples-to-apples unit-econ numbers for Aurum. High-level observations from the call:

- Hyperscaler A quoted ~ $58 / 1M tokens for the same model class (their public managed endpoint).
- During the demo we highlighted three Redwood differentiators that materially change per-token economics: continuous batching (higher throughput at sustained QPS), prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts (significant savings for conversational flows), and model quantization profiles tuned per- workload.

Our rough estimate (back-of-envelope) for Aurum's demo workload was ~ $32 / 1M tokens assuming: batch size ~8 average, ~70% cache hit on prefixes, and INT8 quantization on the last-hop model. That estimate is captured in the attached econ workbook (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-econ-sheet.xlsx).

To make this rigorous we propose a short lab with the following test matrix:

1) Baseline per-1M tokens: batch sizes = [1, 8, 32]; quantization = [fp16, int8]; run each for 1M output tokens.
2) Cache hit sensitivity: run at cache hit rates = [20%, 50%, 80%] to show delta on cost and observed token reduction.
3) Latency profile: capture p50/p95/p99 latency for each config — target SLO is p95 < 500ms for the interactive path.
4) Failure/fallback: measure the cost and latency when we fallback to a cheaper/model-variant under load (to show graceful degradation economics).

What we need from Aurum:
- A sample traffic trace or a small representative conversation set (1k sessions) or permission to replay the live trace (anonymized).
- Any hard latency SLOs you must meet.
- Confirmation that we can run 1M token jobs in a test project in your region (us-west).

Proposed timeline: we can turn around the first-pass results in 3 business days once we have the trace and test access, and a full sensitivity sweep within 5 business days.

I attached a starter CSV (cache-batch-sensitivity-results.csv) with the fields we'll use to report per-run: run_id, batch_size, cache_hit, quant, tokens_out, tokens_in, p95_latency_ms, infra_cost_usd.

Next steps: please confirm we have permission to run the tests on the sample trace (or send the trace), and which confidentiality/contracting contacts we should loop in for the test environment access.

Thanks — looking forward to tightening the numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-econ-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), cache-batch-sensitivity-results.csv (data template)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference economics — hyperscaler comparison and lab asks

Kim / Jane —

Thanks Kim, great recap. A few clarifying notes from an ops/runtime perspective so the lab produces actionable TCO numbers:

- Runtime config: we'll run the tests on the same model family you evaluated today (mvpt-large) with two execution paths: INT8 + cache enabled, and FP16 + cache disabled. That will isolate quantization impact from caching.
- Token accounting: we'll log tokens_in (requests) vs tokens_out (generated). For caching we'll report effective tokens_charged = tokens_out * (1 - cache_hit).
- Batch behavior: use a synthetic arrival process that matches Aurum's 95th percentile QPS (you provided ~18 QPS in the call). We'll sweep batch sizes and measure how often batching increases p95 vs batch1 (lower latency but higher cost).
- Cost model: infra_cost_usd will include GPU runtime + ephemeral infra + infra amortized per-run. We'll normalize per-1M tokens.

Suggested immediate next step: run a single 1M-token run with batch=8, cache_hit=50%, INT8 to validate the numbers in Kim's sheet. If that aligns with Aurum's internal expectations, run full sweep.

I'll prepare the run scripts (benchmark harness + token accounting) and push to the shared Drive link. Jane — once we have the trace/access, can your infra team open test project access for redwood-testing@aurum.com (least privilege)?

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
